title: Negative caching and TTL jitter for city pages
problem: Bots probe /cities/<id> with random ids, and every miss for a missing city goes to the database. And after a deploy, thousands of city keys are cached in the same second, so they all expire in the same second. Write get_city with negative caching and jittered TTLs, plus the hook that makes newly created cities visible at once.
requirements: A city that exists is cached as JSON with ex = POSITIVE_TTL + rng.randrange(JITTER)
A city that doesn't exist is cached as a 'not found' marker with ex = NEGATIVE_TTL (no jitter)
A cached 'not found' returns None without calling load_city
on_city_created(r, city_id) removes any cached entry for that id
If load_city raises, nothing is cached and the exception propagates
Call rng.randrange exactly once per positive cache fill (use the rng argument, not random directly)
contract:
get_city(r, load_city, city_id: int, rng=random) -> dict | None
on_city_created(r, city_id: int) -> None
expectedBehavior: get_city(r, load, 404) returns None and caches the marker for 30 s; a second call returns None without calling load. get_city(r, load, 1, rng=random.Random(1)) caches Paris with TTL 600 + random.Random(1).randrange(60).
edgeCases: Second lookup of a missing id within NEGATIVE_TTL: no database call
A city created after its id was cached as missing
City dicts with falsy fields ('' name, 0 population) are hits, not misses
Database error: no marker cached (an outage is not 'not found')
Many keys filled at once: TTLs differ
hints: Conceptual: a cache entry can mean two things now, 'here is the city' and 'there is no such city'. You need a stored value that means 'not found' and can't be confused with a real city or with a miss (the key not existing at all).
Specific: json.dumps(None) is the string 'null', and json.loads('null') is None. So if r.get returns anything that isn't None, you can return json.loads of it directly: a city dict or None.

Implementation: raw = r.get(key); if raw is not None: return json.loads(raw). Otherwise city = load_city(city_id); if city is None, set json.dumps(None) with ex=NEGATIVE_TTL; else set json.dumps(city) with ex=POSITIVE_TTL + rng.randrange(JITTER). on_city_created just deletes the key.
evaluation: The 'not found' marker can't collide with a real city
The negative TTL is shorter than the positive one, so new cities show up quickly even without the hook
An exception from load_city is never cached as 'not found'
